verdicts.reason: A: the CTA sits top-left above everything, so the reading order is upside down; one can is enlarged while two are shrunk to tiny cans stranded in the bottom-left; the headline, flavour names (in reverse order), body, promo and descriptors are crammed into one small block with no spacing; and the flavour names are cut off from their descriptors. B has the same breakage: the flavour names are nearly as big as the wrapped headline, the descriptors are detached and out of order, the promo line runs into the bubbles, and two tiny cans float at the bottom. B is marginally less bad because its two-column split gives larger, more legible text and a better-balanced canvas.

A keeps the original structure on the square canvas: logo, headline, three equal cans each with its name and descriptor, body copy, CTA and promo line, all centred with even spacing. The only flaws are slightly wide side margins and a little dead space at the bottom. B breaks the design: the CTA sits top-right ahead of the headline, one can is blown up while two are tiny and orphaned bottom-right, the flavour names compete with the headline and are separated from their scrambled descriptors, and the text column is jammed while large areas sit empty.
